UNHCR said more than 2,400 arrived in the past week, most of them women, children and older people. Djibouti, a country of about a million people already hosting some 36,000 refugees, is preparing for up to 10,000. About 2,000 of the displaced are pregnant women, and around 22 million people in Yemen need assistance. The displacement widened after the Houthi seizure of the Red Sea coast.
דווח ב־UNHCR / WHO / TRT World (תדרוך ז׳: Sandrine Desamours, the UNHCR representative in Djibouti, told a briefing at the Palais des Nations that about 3,000 people had crossed Bab al-Mandab in small boats in under a week, landing at Obock, Khor Angar, Moulhoule and Godoria. More than half were women and children, and some were families displaced for a second time since 2015. The Markazi refugee village, with capacity for 5,000, was already hosting more than 2,700 Yemenis and 1,500 Eritreans, with about 270 more staying with host families. The Djiboutian government is preparing for up to 10,000. UNHCR's Djibouti operation is 15% funded, short about $5.1 million, and its Yemen operation 18% funded, needing a further $14 million for shelter and site management. WHO spokesman Tarik Jasarevic said only 60% of 5,415 health facilities assessed in Yemen were fully functioning. Reported by UNHCR, WHO and TRT World.
